Sector briefs

Logistics & Supply Chain: the Saudi market-entry brief

Ports, hubs, free zones and customs: how to choose where to build.

For operators, shippers and investors. It lays out the network you will be working in, how to compare locations and partners, the customs and licensing questions to settle early, and how to test a route before you commit.

What's inside

  • How the sector works, in plain words
  • Five forces driving demand
  • Ways in: contract logistics with an existing operator, joint venture with a local operator, build or lease your own facility
  • 5 rules and approvals to check early
  • Who you will meet: port and terminal operators, freight forwarders and customs brokers, local trucking and last-mile providers
  • 5 common mistakes, and how to avoid them
  • A 90-day plan, in three phases
  • 8 questions to ask before you commit

Who it is for

  • Leadership and business-development teams weighing a Saudi entry
  • Investors who want to understand a sector before they meet partners
  • Teams that have just entered and want to check they have not missed something

A taste of it

Saudi Arabia sits between three continents, and it is investing in ports, rail, airports, logistics parks and free zones to make the most of that position. For operators, shippers and investors, the opportunity is real. So is the complexity: location, customs, licensing and network partners all affect your economics.
